newsitem.title: UK: British nurses charged with murder in Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: British nurses charged with murder in Saudi Arabia.

text.p: Two British nurses working in Saudi Arabia have been charged with the murder of an Australian colleague, the Saudi embassy in London said on Tuesday.
Deborah Kim Parry, 41, and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, had been held for questioning over the murder of nurse Yvonne Gilford, 55, at the King Fahd Military Medical Complex in Dhahran.

"They are going to meet with a representative of the British embassy later in the day," the Saudi embassy said in a statement. "There will be a trial which will examine the case in detail...The Saudi government will ensure justice for all concerned."
The case almost caused a diplomatic crisis when Saudi officials at first refused requests from British diplomats to visit the two nurses in custody in Dhahran.
But the London Foreign Office said Saudi authorities had finally agreed to a request by local embassy staff to visit the two women, who have been held since Friday.
Gilford's body was found in her room on December 11. She had been stabbed four times, battered with a hammer and smothered.
Human rights groups have expressed concern over the detention of the two women, who could face public beheading if they are convicted of murder.
The 1,600 staff at the base had initially been refused permission to leave and passports were taken from foreigners. But British diplomats later said passports had been returned.
